sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: A geometric figure scaled by factor $k = 3$ has an original side length of $6\mathrm{\ cm}$. What is the corresponding image length? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.target: The unit circle and angles of any magnitude
questions.answer: Final Answer: $18\mathrm{\ cm}$. Multiplying the original length by the scale factor gives $6 \times 3 = 18\mathrm{\ cm}$.
questions.explanation: Multiplying the original length by the scale factor gives $6 \times 3 = 18\mathrm{\ cm}$.

questions.q: On the coordinate plane, a line with slope $m = 2$ passes through $(0, 7)$. What is its $y$-coordinate when $x = 2$? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.target: The unit circle and angles of any magnitude
questions.answer: Final Answer: $11$. Substituting $x = 2$ into $y = 2x + 7$ gives $y = 2(2) + 7 = 11$.

questions.q: In $\Delta  ABC$ studying the unit circle and angles of any magnitude, $m\angle A = 37^\circ$ and $m\angle B = 59^\circ$. What is $m\angle C$? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.target: The unit circle and angles of any magnitude
questions.answer: Final Answer: $84^\circ$. Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (37^\circ + 59^\circ) = 84^\circ$.
questions.explanation: Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (37^\circ + 59^\circ) = 84^\circ$.

sections.heading: Part II — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Multi-Step Application (8–14)

questions.q: On the coordinate plane, a line with slope $m = 2$ passes through $(0, 7)$. What is its $y$-coordinate when $x = 4$? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.target: The unit circle and angles of any magnitude
questions.answer: Final Answer: $15$. Substituting $x = 4$ into $y = 2x + 7$ gives $y = 2(4) + 7 = 15$.

questions.q: For the model $f(x) = 5x + 8$ in trigonometric identities, evaluate $f(2)$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $18$. Substitute $x = 2$: $f(2) = 5(2) + 8 = 18$.

questions.q: Find the positive solutions to the quadratic equation $x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $x = 1$ and $x = 4$. Factoring $(x - 1)(x - 4) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 1$ and $x = 4$.

questions.q: A data set recorded for trigonometric identities consists of the four values $\{16, 20, 24, 30\}$. What is the arithmetic mean? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $22.5$. The sum is $16 + 20 + 24 + 30 = 90$, and dividing by $4$ gives $22.5$.
questions.explanation: The sum is $16 + 20 + 24 + 30 = 90$, and dividing by $4$ gives $22.5$.

questions.q: For the model $f(x) = 5x + 8$ in trigonometric identities, evaluate $f(3)$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $23$. Substitute $x = 3$: $f(3) = 5(3) + 8 = 23$.

questions.q: Find the positive solutions to the quadratic equation $x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $x = 2$ and $x = 5$. Factoring $(x - 2)(x - 5) = 0$ yields the roots $x = 2$ and $x = 5$.

questions.q: For the model $f(x) = 5x + 8$ in trigonometric identities, evaluate $f(4)$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $28$. Substitute $x = 4$: $f(4) = 5(4) + 8 = 28$.
